name: Rethink Priorities: animal welfare (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Changes others' spending: the charities of each cause it informs, read live, bring their own countries.
summary: Rethink Priorities researches and coordinates farmed and wild animal welfare work for funders and advocacy groups; this model covers its animal welfare department in 2025 ($1.40M, $2.4M with its share of central costs; the projects it fiscally sponsors are their own and left out). Its research helped funders deploy almost $10M of EU farmed animal welfare grants, of which we judge 15% changed, and its strategy forum gathered 26 advocacy groups, of whose budgets we judge 2% changed: about $2.2M a year steered, all money that would have gone to animals anyway, valued at its gain from an ordinary animal charity to the animal charities on the rankings, live. At the defaults that is about 0.0001 years of healthy life per $1,000, as small as the animal charities whose work it shapes at the site's animal weights, with the next dollar at 40% of the past average; the result moves most with the animal weights, the shares changed (our judgments) and its next-dollar figure, and the whole department is discounted for missing data, since nobody has measured what the funders did differently.

sections.title: Reach

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Share of management and fundraising that serves Rethink Priorities' own research departments
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The accounts don't split management and fundraising between its own departments and the sponsored projects. Its own budget table for 2025 puts 'core operations' at $1.915M (estimated expenses, which it says include 'some additional support for our Special Projects'), with the development team outside the table; $1.915M plus most of the $0.64M of fundraising is about 70% of the $3.34M of management and fundraising in the accounts. 70% (50% to 100%): the low end has the sponsored projects' fees carry half the central costs, the high end none.

source.title: Rethink Priorities, 2025 Results, 2026 Plans and Funding Needs (November 2025)
source.quote: Enabled major funders to more confidently deploy almost $10 million in grants toward EU farmed animal welfare advocacy

rows.explainer: Its own report of the year's main outcome for funders: grants of 'almost $10 million' that major funders deployed 'more confidently' after its work on EU farmed animal welfare advocacy. Its own count, no list of the grants published; 8 to 10 million.

rows.label: Share of those grants whose allocation its research changed
rows.explainer: Our judgment. 'More confidently deploy' says the funders had planned the grants: the research changed how much, to whom or how fast for part of them, not whether animal advocacy was funded. 15% (5% to 40%), anchored on the shared own-effect share for a meta organisation without a survey (30%, 15–45%, facts/meta.json) halved because these are professional funders with their own staff and other advisers, against the share an evaluator's recommendation changes for its donors.

source.quote: Convened movement leaders from 26 organizations for the fourth Animal Advocacy Strategy Forum, which helped advance 10 strategic initiatives

rows.explainer: Movement leaders from 26 organisations at its fourth strategy forum, which it says advanced 10 strategic initiatives; its fish welfare forum (18 organisations) and insect welfare coordination largely overlap with them and are counted through this group, not added.

rows.label: Yearly budget of an organisation it convened (US$)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the forum gathers the larger farmed animal advocacy groups and some small ones; ACE's Recommended Charities run from about $0.5M (Dansk Vegetarisk Forening's animal work, Aquatic Life Institute) to over $10M (The Humane League), most between $1M and $5M. A median of $1.5M (0.5 to 5 million).

rows.label: Share of a convened organisation's yearly budget whose use its coordination and research changed
rows.explainer: Our judgment: a forum, a roadmap or a strategy report shifts a small part of what an organisation does in a year (a campaign target, a new species ask, a country chosen); 2% (0.5% to 6%), below the funders' share because each organisation's plans are its own and the work is shared with the other organisations at the table.

rows.explainer: The two ways its animal welfare research and coordination change what others spend: funders' grants and the convened organisations' own budgets, each at the share it changed. All of it would have been spent on animals anyway (shifted, not new money).

rows.label: Value of a dollar to animal welfare charities (live), units of value
rows.explainer: The money its animal welfare work changes stays in farmed and wild animal welfare (EU advocacy grants, advocacy groups' budgets); no split by recipient is published, so it is valued at the animal welfare charities on the rankings, equal weights (#cause:animal-welfare, the site's rule for money to a cause with no recipient named).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where the money its research changed went: the cause's charities on this site, live (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: an ordinary charity of its cause, as 1× GiveDirectly is in global health), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the shared rule for an organisation that moves money within a cause other than global health (animal-welfare). Shifted money was going to be given anyway, to an ordinary charity of the same cause; it is credited only for the gain. An ordinary charity stands to its cause's charities on the rankings as GiveDirectly (GiveWell's model, times a shared multiple, 1×, from 0 to 3×) stands to global health's: GiveDirectly's live result over the global-health charities' (#cause:global-health), times the animal-welfare charities' (#cause:animal-welfare), all live under your values.

rows.label: Share of money moved that is new money
rows.explainer: The site's one figure for every meta charity. Not used on the path here: the money Rethink Priorities' research changes is funders' and organisations' money that would have been spent anyway, all shifted, valued at its gain only (as GiveWell's model values Open Philanthropy's money).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone. Not on the path here: all of the money counted is shifted (moved_value).

rows.label: Value of the career changes (units of value)
Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the share of the gain counted that is real. Research that changes an allocation can point the wrong way or overstate the difference between options, and funders' own staff check it; 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), the template's figure for research and policy work, with a lower end for strategy research whose results nobody measures.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1: what the funders and organisations would have done without the research is netted out in each branch's share of the money it changed (Convention 5: one question, asked once).

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: 1: other advisers and the funders' own staff are netted out in each branch's share of the money it changed, which counts only the part its research changed.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin (the site's missing-data step, docs/normalization.md 2.12): the money informed is its own report or our judgment and the share it changed is our judgment, with no follow-up of what the funders did differently; Rethink Priorities says it reports outputs and is building an evaluation of its downstream effects. Applied to every branch.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above, applied to the money its research changed and to the empty policy branch.

rows.label: Side effects of its animal welfare work beyond the money counted, as a share of its value
rows.explainer: Good and harm the two branches leave out. Positive: its published research used by funders and advocates it never hears from (its 2025 outputs were cited by Animal Charity Evaluators, Open Philanthropy and Ambitious Impact), the farmed-animal forecasts and wild animal intervention database, insect and shrimp welfare asks taken up by groups outside the forum, and its earlier welfare-range and sentience work that funders (and this site's animal weights) still use. Negative: staff time of the organisations it convenes, and research that points funders the wrong way. 20% (−10% to +60%), our judgment, above ACE's 10% because more of its work is published research than an evaluator's.

rows.label: Value of the money its research changed (units of value)
rows.explainer: The money its work changed, all shifted, at the gain of the cause's charities over an ordinary animal charity (moved_dollar_value − prior_dollar_value, the shared rule for money all shifted), after the adjustments and with the side effects.

rows.label: Total value (units of value)
rows.explainer: The policy branch is empty; the money its research changed counts its own adjustments (moved_value), careers are 0.
